positive_recovery.structural-local-and-lambda-annotations: Grouped and tuple type annotations use canonical lexer lookahead that the editor GLR parser approximates; highlighting may recover this fixture.

negative_parse_groups.reason: Tree-sitter's contextual keyword lexer can recover reserved words as names in positions where the compiler's lexer refuses them.
Compiler declaration actions enforce modifier ordering, multiplicity and applicability, constant initialization and proof-signature restrictions; highlighting retains their token structure.
Compiler pattern actions enforce constructor capitalization, qualification, nullary spelling and complete binding shape; highlighting retains the enclosing expression or pattern structure.
The compiler's lexical admission rules refuse null and null-conditional spellings; the editor can recover them as identifiers, propagation and member punctuation.
Canonical annotation lookahead rejects type-shaped bare locals; the editor's GLR alternatives can retain an expression-shaped recovery.
The editor raw-string scanner recognizes exact quote delimiters; opening/closing-line layout and content indentation remain compiler lexical checks.
Interpolation highlighting preserves strings and balanced holes while nonempty expressions and format specifiers remain compiler lexical checks.

outside_editor_envelope: Invalid UTF-8 and compiler resource-limit fixtures retain their compiler refusals; they are not accepted as editor syntax or projected beyond the declared 65,536-byte source limit.
